reconciled_candidates.label: Text Summarization Objectives
reconciled_candidates.description: Text summarization aims to condense information from one or more source texts into a shorter version that preserves the main ideas and important content, serving as a tool for accessibility and efficient information retrieval.
coverage_criteria: Student can state the primary goal of text summarization and list its benefits for readers and producers.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate introduces the core purpose of text summarization, a distinct foundational concept that stands alone.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source introduces summarization objectives from both reader and producer perspectives, emphasizing the need for condensed information in the face of abundant data.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a foundational concept that can be assessed with a single definition and purpose question.

reconciled_candidates.label: Mono-document vs Multi-document Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: Summarization can be classified by the number of input documents: mono-document summarization produces a summary from a single text, while multi-document summarization synthesizes information from multiple related documents, often dealing with greater information volume.
coverage_criteria: Student can differentiate between mono-document and multi-document summarization and provide an example scenario for each.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate presents a clear binary classification, distinct from other dimensions, making it a standalone teachable concept.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source explicitly describes these two types under the classification by number of processed texts, noting multi-document algorithms are very important for processing large information sets.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This binary classification is straightforward and can be checked with a compare/contrast question.

reconciled_candidates.label: Extractive vs Abstractive Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: Extractive summarization selects and concatenates unchanged sentences from the source text, while abstractive summarization may rephrase or generate new sentences, potentially altering structure and meaning, and requiring more complex NLP.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain the difference between extractive and abstractive summarization, and identify which is more complex and why.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This core classification differentiates the two main summarization approaches, a standalone concept essential for understanding the field.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source defines extratos (extractive) and abstratos (abstractive), provides the example of a news summary, and discusses that abstractive is highly complex, leading to more research in extractive methods.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a central classification in summarization, checkable with a definition and example question.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video explicitly defines extractive summarization at [01:54] and contrasts it with abstractive summarization at [02:54].
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a foundational definition that can be assessed with two short questions, making it an appropriate checkable concept.

source_metadata.source_name: Text Summarization of COVID-19 Medical Articles using BERT and GPT-2 (Research Paper Walkthrough)

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video describes abstractive summarization and its challenges at [02:54], emphasizing the need for semantic representation and creative generation.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Distinguishing abstractive from extractive summarization is a key learning point, testable with direct questions.

source_metadata.source_name: Text Summarization of COVID-19 Medical Articles using BERT and GPT-2 (Research Paper Walkthrough)

reconciled_candidates.label: Indicative vs Informative Summaries
reconciled_candidates.description: Indicative summaries provide a vague idea of the content and cannot replace the source, while informative summaries preserve the main content and can act as substitutes, allowing users to understand the subject without reading the full text.
coverage_criteria: Student can distinguish between indicative and informative summaries and explain when each is more appropriate.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This classification by output detail is a distinct, practical concept that stands alone for assessment.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source describes these two types, noting indicative are easier to produce automatically but less useful, while informative are more valuable but harder to evaluate.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This distinction is a practical classification that can be assessed with a definition and use-case question.

reconciled_candidates.label: Generic vs User-Oriented Summaries
reconciled_candidates.description: Generic summaries present the most important information without considering the user's background, while user-oriented summaries tailor the content based on the user's knowledge, providing context for novices or novelty for experts.
coverage_criteria: Student can differentiate between generic and user-oriented summaries and describe a scenario where user-oriented would be beneficial.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This classification based on user adaptation is a separate dimension from other taxonomies, meriting its own concept.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source introduces this classification, explaining that user-oriented summaries can be customized to the user's knowledge level, giving the example of a layperson vs. an expert.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a single dimension of classification that can be checked with a straightforward comparison question.

reconciled_candidates.label: Supervised vs Unsupervised Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: Supervised summarization treats sentence inclusion as a classification task trained on labeled examples, while unsupervised summarization uses pre-defined features and heuristics to determine sentence importance without needing training data.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain the difference between supervised and unsupervised approaches to summarization and give an example of each.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This learning-based classification is distinct and forms a standalone concept that can be checked with focused questions.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source presents this classification, describing supervised as a classification task and unsupervised as using specialized algorithms with a predefined set of features.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a method-level distinction that can be assessed with a definition and characteristic question.

reconciled_candidates.label: Intermediate Representation in Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: The first step of summarization processing is creating an intermediate representation that captures the main aspects of the text, such as topic representations using word frequency tables or more complex indicators.
coverage_criteria: The student can define intermediate representation and describe one common method.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate represents a distinct step in the summarization process.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source details that even the simplest systems derive an intermediate representation, and topic representation approaches convert text into topics with word weights.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a distinct, fundamental step in summarization that can be checked with a single definition and example question.

reconciled_candidates.label: Sentence Scoring for Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: After intermediate representation, each sentence receives a score indicating its importance, often based on how well it expresses key topics or a combination of indicator evidence, sometimes using machine learning.
coverage_criteria: The student can explain the purpose of sentence scoring and describe a common method.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate captures a distinct step following representation.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source states that after intermediate representation, each sentence is scored for importance, with topic-based scoring related to how well it expresses the document's topics.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a key processing step that can be assessed with a description question, distinct from the representation and selection steps.

reconciled_candidates.label: Sentence Selection Algorithms
reconciled_candidates.description: The summarization system selects a set of high-scoring sentences to form a summary, using greedy approaches that recalculate importance considering redundancy, or global optimization maximizing importance and coherence.
coverage_criteria: The student can describe the goal of sentence selection and outline one approach.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate covers the selection step, distinct from scoring.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source explains that in the third step, the system selects the best combination of important sentences, with methods like recalculating scores based on similarity to avoid redundancy, or global selection with constraints.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a core algorithmic step that can be checked with a description of the selection process.

reconciled_candidates.label: Reformulation in Abstractive Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: In abstractive summarization, a final reformulation step rewrites or paraphrases the selected content to produce a fluent summary, often using natural language generation.
coverage_criteria: The student can explain when reformulation is applied and its role.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate covers a step unique to abstractive summarization.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source notes that reformulation is applied only in cases of abstractive summarization, as shown in the figure and described in the text.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a specific step distinct from the others, applicable only to one type, making it a clear checkable concept.

reconciled_candidates.label: Compression Rate in Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: Compression rate defines the size of the summary relative to the source text; e.g., a 60% compression rate means the summary will be 40% of the original length.
coverage_criteria: The student can define compression rate and calculate target summary length.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate covers a key parameter of summarization output.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source introduces compression rate as the factor that guides the summarization result, giving a concrete example of 60% compression.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a simple, checkable parameter that can be assessed with a definition and calculation question.

reconciled_candidates.label: Extractive Summarization Example with Python and NLTK
reconciled_candidates.description: An extractive summarization workflow in Python using urllib, BeautifulSoup, NLTK for tokenization and stopword removal, then scoring sentences by word frequency to select the top sentences.
coverage_criteria: The student can list the main steps: fetching data, parsing HTML, tokenizing, removing stopwords, creating frequency distribution, scoring sentences, and selecting top sentences.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate provides a concrete practical example of extractive summarization.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source provides a detailed 10-step Python code example of extractive summarization, with explanations, illustrating a practical application of the concepts.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a concrete, checkable example that can be assessed by having the student outline the steps or identify the purpose of key libraries.

reconciled_candidates.label: BERT Sentence Embeddings and K-Medoid Clustering for Extractive Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: Pre-trained BERT models convert sentences into fixed-length embeddings, which are then clustered using K-medoid to select representative sentences as the extractive summary, ensuring selected sentences are actual text excerpts.
coverage_criteria: The student can explain how BERT creates sentence embeddings and how K-medoid clustering selects sentences.
The student can contrast K-means and K-medoid for this task.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: These candidates describe the embedding and clustering approach as a combined technique for extractive summarization.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video introduces the extractive summarization pipeline at [05:10], explicitly describing how BERT transforms sentences into 768-dimensional vectors.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Sentence embeddings are a core NLP technique; this concept checks understanding of their role in summarization with two focused questions.

source_metadata.source_name: Text Summarization of COVID-19 Medical Articles using BERT and GPT-2 (Research Paper Walkthrough)

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video details K-medoid clustering at [07:01] and its application within the extractive summarization pipeline at [05:10].
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Understanding why and how K-medoid is used for extractive summarization is specific enough to be assessed with a short explanation.

source_metadata.source_name: Text Summarization of COVID-19 Medical Articles using BERT and GPT-2 (Research Paper Walkthrough)

reconciled_candidates.label: Fine-tuning GPT-2 for Abstractive Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: GPT-2 is fine-tuned with a multi-loss strategy combining language modeling and multiple-choice prediction, using special tokens like <summarize> and keywords as input, with masked self-attention ensuring auto-regressive generation.
coverage_criteria: The student can describe the two training objectives (language modeling and multiple-choice) and their weighting.
The student can explain the role of special tokens and masked self-attention in the fine-tuning process.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: These candidates together detail the GPT-2 fine-tuning strategy and its key components.

anchors.locator: [13:48] Training Strategy of the Abstractive Summarization GPT-2

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video thoroughly explains the training strategy, input format, special tokens, and loss weighting at [13:48] and [17:13].
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This multi-loss approach is a key innovation of the paper, and can be assessed with multiple questions about its components.

source_metadata.source_name: Text Summarization of COVID-19 Medical Articles using BERT and GPT-2 (Research Paper Walkthrough)

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video mentions masked self-attention as part of the training strategy intuition at [17:51], noting it blocks information from the right.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Masked self-attention is a fundamental mechanism in transformers; its purpose can be checked with a concise explanation.

source_metadata.source_name: Text Summarization of COVID-19 Medical Articles using BERT and GPT-2 (Research Paper Walkthrough)

anchors.locator: [13:48] Training Strategy of the Abstractive Summarization GPT-2

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video describes the use of `<summarize>` to separate keywords and the summary at [13:48] and how GPT-2 learns this cue at [17:13].
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: The role of control tokens is a concrete, teachable detail of language model fine-tuning that can be checked with a short answer.

source_metadata.source_name: Text Summarization of COVID-19 Medical Articles using BERT and GPT-2 (Research Paper Walkthrough)

reconciled_candidates.label: Keyword Extraction for Abstractive Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: In the abstractive summarization pipeline, important keywords (nouns and verbs) are automatically extracted using techniques like NLTK POS tagging or fine-tuned BERT, providing a condensed representation for the summarization model.
coverage_criteria: The student can name at least one method for keyword extraction and explain how keywords are used in the summarization input.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate covers a preprocessing step distinct from the model itself.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video explains keyword extraction with NLTK and BERT at [12:22] and its role in the abstractive summarization pipeline.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Keyword extraction is a critical preprocessing step whose function and methods can be checked with two direct questions.

source_metadata.source_name: Text Summarization of COVID-19 Medical Articles using BERT and GPT-2 (Research Paper Walkthrough)

reconciled_candidates.label: Data Scarcity in Domain-Specific Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: Low availability of domain-specific data (e.g., only 35k pairs in COVID-19 research vs 286k in general datasets) and rare terminology can hinder effective fine-tuning of large models like BERT and GPT-2.
coverage_criteria: The student can quantify the data size challenge and explain why limited domain data degrades fine-tuning.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate highlights a practical challenge in applying summarization to niche domains.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video explicitly discusses the low-resource challenge at [04:13], including dataset size comparison and terminology mismatch.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept highlights a practical constraint in NLP projects, and students can be asked to recall specific numbers and reasons.

source_metadata.source_name: Text Summarization of COVID-19 Medical Articles using BERT and GPT-2 (Research Paper Walkthrough)

reconciled_candidates.label: Future Direction: Hybrid Extractive-Abstractive Summarization
reconciled_candidates.description: A suggested future approach is to feed sentences extracted by extractive summarization directly into an abstractive model, potentially improving summary quality by providing richer context.
coverage_criteria: The student can summarize this future work suggestion and discuss one potential benefit.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate presents a forward-looking idea that synthesizes the two summarization paradigms.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video concludes with this suggestion at [21:16], explicitly proposing the combination of extractive and abstractive methods.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This forward-looking idea encourages synthesis of the two summarization approaches and can be assessed with a short reflective question.
